notes:
POC started Sept -> Nov. Short summary:
- Use case: low-latency ranking + personalization in ad stack (tail 95th <= 60ms target for inferencing pipeline).
- Initially favored Redwood for routing/fallback story, KV cache demos looked good.
- They required VPC + SOC2 + EU data residency for EU customer subset.
- POC environment: 2 dedicated nodes, 40M tokens/day simulated traffic.
- Key quote from Head of ML (Aaron Li): "If we can't hit 50-60ms p95 consistently, it's a non-starter — ad auctions won't wait."
- Mid-POC: engineering reported intermittent 150-200ms spikes on long-context sessions; Ops suspected kernel mismatch with their transformers fork.
- Security ran a deep-dive; asked about upgrade path for private images and KMS audit logs. Our answers were ok but they wanted a formal runbook and independent pen-test report (asked to provide by 2024-11-30).
- Meanwhile competitor Together offered an on-prem + unified billing demo and an aggressive price on quantized model serving. Sales told us Together offered a 6-month pilot at lower list price.
- Dec 12: procurement paused due to Q1 budget freeze at client; execs prioritized core ad budget.
- Jan 08: Twinleaf notified Redwood via SE that they chose Together after cost/ops review. Primary reasons: price + perceived faster on-prem integration + existing relationship with partner integrator.
- They emphasized "faster time to first model in infra" and "single bill". No technical objections left besides the latency spikes.
- Actionable: capture detailed POC logs and the kernel trace around long-context runs; ask for Together POC benchmarks; schedule win-back call after 6 months.
